name: Move with Urgency
definition: Urgency is a sense of crisis. We treat inaction as a threat to survival. We learn by doing and do not delay decisions to seek a 'perfect' solution.

rows.situation: When the decision can be undone cheaply
rows.under: Runs it through the same review as a decision that cannot be undone.
rows.justRight: Decides now, makes the way back explicit, and moves.
rows.over: Treats an expensive one-way decision as reversible, and cannot get back.

rows.under: Waits for the study. The window closes during it.
rows.justRight: Acts on the information that would change the decision, and starts learning by doing.
rows.over: Acts before reading the one number that was already sitting there.

rows.situation: When nothing is technically on fire
rows.under: Treats a calm quarter as a safe quarter.
rows.justRight: Treats standing still as losing, and holds the pace when there is no crisis to force it.
rows.over: Manufactures crisis constantly, until urgency stops meaning anything to the team.

rows.situation: When a problem needs someone senior tonight
rows.under: Waits for the morning and the normal channel.
rows.justRight: Wakes people up. A few interrupted evenings cost less than a lost week.
rows.over: Escalates everything immediately, and burns the channel you need for the real thing.

rows.situation: When moving fast has started producing defects
rows.under: Keeps the pace and lets quality slide out of view.
rows.justRight: Keeps the pace and puts the check in the path, so speed does not depend on nobody making a mistake.
rows.over: Slows to a crawl after one defect and stops shipping anything.

rows.situation: When a decision has been open for weeks
rows.under: Lets it stay open. Nobody has forced it.
rows.justRight: Sets a date, names who decides, and makes the call on that date with what is known.
rows.over: Forces decisions before the people who have to live with them have been asked.
